sentences.text: Huaxiagnathus is an extinct coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China.
The largest known individual reached about 1.8 meters in length, making it one of the largest compsognathids.
It is distinguished by a long premaxillary process overlapping the antorbital fossa and a hand as long as the combined humerus and radius.
The holotype specimen was collected from the Yixian Formation at Dabangou Village near Beipiao City in western Liaoning Province.
Cladistic analysis places Huaxiagnathus at the base of Compsognathidae due to its unspecialized arms.
In 2004, Hwang et al. classified Huaxiagnathus as the most basal known compsognathid based on its unspecialized forearm.
Huaxiagnathus is classified within the family Compsognathidae.
Huaxiagnathus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Huaxiagnathus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
A 2024 study by Andrea Cau questioned whether Huaxiagnathus belongs within Compsognathidae, noting it was known only from immature specimens.
Cau and Paterna (2025) proposed that Sinotyrannus is a mature form of Huaxiagnathus, suggesting the latter name has priority.
